arguments.premise_synthesis: The speech argues that interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve are now priced in at an 87% chance at the next meeting. Furthermore, the Fed's implementation notes indicate that starting December 1, the Fed will roll over principal payments from its Treasury holdings and reinvest principal payments from agency mortgage-backed securities into Treasury bills. Additionally, central banks around the world have recently stopped raising rates or begun cutting rates, collectively pointing to a global monetary easing cycle that increases liquidity and supports higher asset prices.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The speech establishes that the ongoing global monetary easing cycle, including anticipated Fed rate cuts and reinvestment policies, will increase liquidity and support higher asset prices, reinforcing the perception of a resilient economy.

They won't let them bleed off their balance sheet anymore. But it doesn't stop there because again starting on December 1st, they will also be reinvesting all principal payments from the Fed holdings of agency mortgage back securities into Treasury bills.
